value.source_text: The nomenclature of cyclitols is described in the document entitled â€˜Nomenclature of Cyclitols, Recommendations 1973â€™ (ref. 39).
Cyclitols are cycloalkanes in which three or more ring atoms are each substituted with one hydroxy group.
value.substituent: one hydroxy group per substituted ring atom

value.source_text: Inositols, cyclohexane-1,2,3,4,5,6-hexols, are a specific group of cyclitols.

Inositols have retained names and, together with their O-alkyl, O-aryl, alkanoate/carboxylate esters, and amino derivatives (where NH2 replaces OH) employ the stereodescriptors â€˜Dâ€™ and â€˜Lâ€™ to describe configurations.
Other names of cyclitols are systematic substitutive names whose configurations are described by CIP stereodescriptors.
Various methods are recommended for naming cyclitols.
value.subject: cyclitol naming methods

value.source_text: P-104.2.1 Stereoisomeric inositols are described by adding italicized prefixes at the front of the name ‘inositol’.
Positional numbers described in the following method are indicated in parentheses.
value.subject: positional numbers

value.name_class: names denoted by the stereoisomeric prefixes
value.source_text: Names denoted by the prefixes are preferred.
The absolute configuration of cyclitols is denoted by â€˜Dâ€™ and â€˜Lâ€™ and is determined in the following way.

value.hydroxy_position: above the plane of the ring
value.source_text: For the planar ring representation where the hydroxy group numbered â€˜1â€™ is above the plane of the ring, the configuration â€˜Lâ€™ corresponds to a clockwise numbering, and the configuration â€˜Dâ€™ corresponds to an anticlockwise numbering, as illustrated by the two enantiomeric chiro-inositols above.
The stereodescriptors â€˜Dâ€™ and â€˜Lâ€™ followed by a hyphen are placed before the name of the compound and are preceded by the locant of the defining center, i.e. â€˜1â€™ as shown above.
P-104.2.2 Cyclitols, with the exception of inositols, are named systematically from cyclohexane as the parent using the CIP method and its Sequence Rules for describing stereoisomers.

value.preferred: systematic naming using the CIP method and Sequence Rules
value.source_text: This method is preferred to the method of positional numbers described in P-104.2.3.

P-104.2.3 Locants are assigned to hydroxy groups in cyclitols, and thus the direction of numbering is described, with reference to the steric relations and nature of the substituents attached to the ring.
The substituents lying above the plane of the ring constitute a set, and those lying below another set.

value.objective: relate lowest locants to one substituent set
value.source_text: Lowest locants are related to one set of the substituents according to the following criteria, which are applied successively until a decision is reached:
(a) to the substituents considered as a numerical series, without regard to configuration;
(b) if one set of the substituents is more numerous than the other, to the more numerous;

value.basis: the set denoted by lower numbers
value.source_text: (c) if the sets are equally numerous and one of them can be denoted by lower numbers, to that set;

value.basis: substituents other than unmodified hydroxy groups
value.source_text: (d) to substituents other than unmodified hydroxy groups;
(e) to the substituent first cited in alphanumerical order;

value.basis: designation leading to L rather than D
value.source_text: (f) to those designations that lead to an â€˜Lâ€™ rather than a â€˜Dâ€™ configuration, as determined by the method of P-104.2.1 above (applies to meso compounds only).

value.numerator: set of substituents with the lowest locants
value.source_text: The positional numbers are described by a fractional expression in which the numerator is the set of substituents with the lowest locants, arranged in ascending order, and the denominator is the other set.
Inositols are modified in the same way as carbohydrates to generate names for derivatives.
There is no limit to O-substitution by alkyl (aryl) groups (see P-102.5.6.1).
Hydroxy groups can be exchanged for amino groups using the â€˜deoxyâ€™ operation (see P-102.5.4).
When characteristic groups that are senior to hydroxy groups are put in the place of a hydroxy group, fully substitutive names must be constructed.
However, esters are named as alkanoates/carboxylates.
The numbering of the inositol remains unchanged and the configuration is expressed by an â€˜Lâ€™ or â€˜Dâ€™ stereodescriptor.

value.numbering_relation: may differ from corresponding inositol name
value.source_text: Systematic names may have different numbering from the corresponding inositol name (see examples 2 and 5).

value.scope: derivatives of cyclitols other than inositols
value.source_text: Names for derivatives of cyclitols other than inositols are all constructed by applying the principles, rules, and conventions of substitutive nomenclature described in Chapters P-1 through P-9.
